name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Four additions, no forced item recreation this time (existing watch progress and ids are untouched): (1) Duplicate detection against locally-owned content now checks the whole server, not just the federated library's own folder - a movie you already own in a separate, ordinary library now correctly blocks its federated duplicate from being created. (2) A small icon now appears next to federated items' titles in jellyfin-web (grid cards, lists, and the detail page), so it's clear at a glance which items are streamed from another server - implemented by injecting a small script into index.html at server startup, the same technique other Jellyfin plugins use for client-side additions. (3) Investigated why federated items never showed up in Continue Watching: they already have everything Jellyfin's resume logic needs (stable id, RunTimeTicks, IsVirtualItem=false) - the real cause was that every forced-recreation migration through 0.0.31 wiped saved watch position along with the item it recreated. 0.0.31 was the last of those; resume should now accumulate and persist normally going forward. (4) Direct mode now automatically adapts to network conditions between federated servers, on by default, nothing to configure. Direct mode previously always pulled the source's raw, untranscoded file straight from the remote - fine on a local network, but when the two servers are only connected over the internet, a 25+ Mbps 4K HDR release can exceed the remote's own upload bandwidth and stutter no matter how fast either machine is. A new background check now classifies each server as same-network or internet-only and, only for a confirmed internet link, measures what it can actually sustain (via the remote's own bandwidth-test endpoint, the same mechanism jellyfin-web itself uses) and caps to the largest bitrate that fits - direct play is used whenever there's no evidence a cap is needed, including the entire time before that first check completes, so nothing gets capped speculatively. A fixed manual override and a fully-off switch remain available per server for anyone who wants to pin a specific number.
